answer: Sequential verifiable work resists Sybils by making time itself scarce. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must complete a chain of publicly checkable tasks where each step depends on the last, like a vine that grows one node at a time. Spawning clones does not help, because parallel starts still need the same wall-clock hours, and each chain burns quartz-hard compute that cannot be reused across identities. A yarrow field of fresh clones stays powerless until each one has paid its own time, while an honest finished chain is instantly auditable.
